test(a11y): record the contrast and axe baselines (#76) (#159)

* build(frontend): add @axe-core/playwright for the a11y baseline

axe needs a real browser (happy-dom does not give it enough DOM); it runs in
the e2e suite next to the smoke test. Lock merged into the committed one as
before; npm ci verified.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* test(a11y): record the contrast and axe baselines (#76)

Contrast is information here, not decoration: the design encodes learning
state in ink density. A test parses the tokens out of style.css and pins what
today measures — light ink-50 (3.55-4.13) and ink-35 (2.38-2.77) miss AA on
every layer, dark ink-35 (3.60-4.12) misses it; ink and ink-70 clear it in both
themes. Changing a token now forces a deliberate edit to that table.

axe runs over the four main pages in the e2e suite and pins the violation ids
found today (color-contrast, link-in-text-block) as a ratchet: a new kind fails,
and fixing one sends you back to the table. The review path is exercised with
the keyboard alone (Space reveals, 3 rates) in the smoke test.

docs/conventions.md records the numbers, the options (adjust the tokens, add a
non-colour redundancy, or restrict those levels to non-essential text), that
the axe baseline is not a clean bill of health, and the ruby/screen-reader
limitation (ruby is announced as base then annotation; no aria override).

entry.title: feat(brand): rename the project to Kotobako (#155)
entry.content:
feat(brand): rename the project to Kotobako (#155)

"Studio" pointed at the wrong category. Android Studio, Visual Studio — a
Studio is where you make something. This program does not make anything: it
picks up a line you met, keeps the moment you met it in, and hands the word
back when you are due to see it again. ことばこ is the box those lines go into.

Renaming costs almost nothing today and will never be this cheap again: there
are no releases, no downloads and no users, and GitHub redirects the old
repository URL permanently. The import package stays `kotoba` — the root word is
still exactly right, and it is wired into the Alembic script location, so moving
it would risk the migration history to change a name no user ever sees.

Names that are keys into somebody else's system keep their old value, each with
a comment saying why, because renaming them would strand data that already
exists:

- `MODEL_NAME = "KotobaStudio-v1"` is the note type inside the user's Anki
  collection; renaming it orphans every note exported before today.
- the `kotoba-studio` tag on exported notes keeps a saved `tag:` search working.
- the data directory and the keyring service do move, but the old ones are still
  honoured: `default_data_dir()` returns the pre-rename directory when it exists,
  and a key saved under the old service name is still read. Nothing is copied or
  moved on the user's behalf — an out-of-date directory name is a smaller
  problem than an application that looks like it deleted your cards.

Verified: `make check` green (323 backend, 77 frontend), and the data-directory
fallback exercised over all four combinations of the two directories existing.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)

entry.title: fix(ci): drop the Pages enablement that GITHUB_TOKEN cannot perform (…
entry.content:
fix(ci): drop the Pages enablement that GITHUB_TOKEN cannot perform (#152)

`enablement: true` was meant to save an admin a trip to the settings page. It
cannot: creating a Pages site needs administration:write, which is not among the
scopes GITHUB_TOKEN can be granted, so the job only traded one error for another
— "Get Pages site failed" became "Resource not accessible by integration".

Pages is now switched to the Actions source on this repository and the workflow
deploys, so the option is dead weight. The comment says what a fork has to do
rather than implying the workflow handles it: a configuration that can never
succeed is worse than none, because the next person debugs the wrong thing.

entry.title: fix(docs): let the Pages job enable Pages, and clear the npm advisori…
entry.content:
fix(docs): let the Pages job enable Pages, and clear the npm advisories (#150)

Two failures on main, both from the docs site landing.

configure-pages 404s on a repository where Pages was never switched on, so the
deploy job failed on its first run. `enablement: true` lets the action do the
switch itself — the workflow is already in the repository and already holds
`pages: write`, so making a human visit a settings page to finish the job was
the wrong shape.

Dependabot then failed twice on /docs. VitePress 1.6.4 is the current stable
release and pins Vite 5, which pulls an esbuild carrying dev-server advisories;
VitePress 2 is still alpha, so Dependabot could not resolve a fix and errored
instead of opening a pull request. The advisories are build-time only —
`npm audit --omit=dev` reports nothing and none of that code reaches the
published site — but forcing esbuild >= 0.25 and Vite >= 6.4.3 costs nothing,
builds the same 15 pages, and takes `npm audit` to zero, which keeps a real
alert visible later. docs/README.md says when to drop the overrides.

/docs was also the only npm manifest with no dependabot.yml entry, so security
updates were the only way Dependabot ever touched it. It now gets the same
monthly grouped treatment as /frontend and /backend.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)

entry.title: test(jp): add property tests for the Japanese pipeline (#71) (#149)
entry.content:
test(jp): add property tests for the Japanese pipeline (#71) (#149)

* build(backend): add hypothesis for property tests

Hand-written examples only cover cases someone thought of; the Japanese
pipeline is where the unseen cases hide.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* build(frontend): add fast-check for the furigana property

furigana() is a frontend function, so its property test cannot live in the
backend's hypothesis suite. fast-check is the same idea in JS. The lock was
merged into the committed one (npm 11 inBundle pruning); npm ci verified.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* test(jp): add property tests for the Japanese pipeline (#71)

Random Japanese input now hammers the five functions whose failures are hard to
see: normalize_ocr is idempotent (a second pass that changes text poisons the
hash), parse_subtitles either returns cues or raises ApiError (subtitle files
come from the internet), tokenize covers every non-space character (offsets
drive highlighting), mora_count ignores small kana and stays non-negative, and
pitch's pattern is always one of the four for any accent, out-of-range included.

Two deviations from the issue, both because reality disagreed:

- The tokenize property as literally written is false by design: whitespace is
  not tokenized, which hypothesis found immediately (": :" -> "::"). The test
  now asserts what the pipeline guarantees (no lost non-space characters) and
  the counterexample is frozen as a plain test, offsets included.
- furigana() is a frontend function, so hypothesis cannot reach it; its
  property test lives next to it in vitest with fast-check.

Generators use Japanese characters only (kana, kanji, half-width kana,
punctuation) and are bounded (200 examples, 80 for the tagger) so CI stays fast:
the whole file runs in under two seconds.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

entry.title: feat: give the project a public surface — one icon, a docs site, a re…
entry.content:
feat: give the project a public surface — one icon, a docs site, a rebuilt README (#148)

* feat(brand): give every icon surface the same mascot

Every icon slot carried something different, or nothing: the favicon drew 言
as SVG <text> with a hard-coded Hiragino/Noto font stack — a machine without
those fonts renders a fallback or tofu — the PWA icons were placeholders whose
512 also served as the maskable one with no safe zone, the tray drew its own
shape in code, and the PyInstaller spec set no icon at all, so the Windows
executable and installer shipped with PyInstaller's default.

Now there is one piece of art. Large surfaces use the full illustration;
16-64px use a close crop, because the full scene turns to mush below about
48px while the crop still reads as a face. The tray loads its copy from
package data, so tray, favicon, installer and README cannot drift apart.

- assets/mascot.png, assets/kotoba.ico (16/24/32/48/64/128/256)
- backend/kotoba/data/tray.png, named in core/resources.py like every other
  bundled file; kotoba.spec collects data/*.png alongside data/*.json
- favicon.png replaces favicon.svg (no font dependency), apple-touch-icon.png
- pwa-512-maskable.png gets its own safe zone instead of reusing pwa-512
- manifest theme_color now matches --bg (#f3f2f2) rather than #faf7f1, so the
  splash screen does not seam against the icon

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)

* docs: add a VitePress site and rebuild the README around it

The README carried three audiences at once: a user deciding whether to install
walked through winget commands, the architecture tree and the packaging recipe
before reaching what the program is for. It also had no visual and no badges.

The site's root is docs/ itself, so the same markdown renders on GitHub and on
the site — one copy, no drift, and every link in the README works today rather
than after Pages is switched on.

- README follows the shape AUTO-MAS and MaaFramework use: centred title, badge
  row, then 介绍 / 原理 / 重要声明 / 使用方法 / 参与贡献 / 代码签名 / 隐私政策,
  then 关于 with acknowledgements, contributors, star history and community.
  Every heading and every section body is bilingual, which retires the separate
  collapsed English block.
- New pages moved out of the README: install, guide, mobile, platforms,
  architecture. integrations is new — it documents the outward contract (the
  hook protocol, the subtitle/EPUB/mokuro imports, the Anki exports) and says
  plainly that the ~90 internal REST endpoints are not part of it.
- The site's ground is taken from the icon (#fcf1eb); the accent stays the
  application's gold. Body links use --gold-deep because #b68235 on that ground
  is 3.2:1, under the 4.5:1 running text needs.
- docs.yml builds and deploys to GitHub Pages on changes under docs/.
- conventions.md linked ../AGENTS.md, which resolves on GitHub but is a dead
  link once docs/ is a site root; the build catches this, so it is absolute now.

Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus 5)

entry.content:
fix(e2e): stop the server with the run so CI teardown cannot hang (#147)

* build(frontend): add Playwright for the smoke test

Chromium only: the smoke test is one path, not a browser matrix. The lock was
merged into the committed one by hand again (npm 11 prunes inBundle entries and
then rejects its own output); npm ci is verified.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* test(e2e): smoke the capture-to-review path in a browser (#70)

One Playwright test walks the path no unit test proves end to end: create a
source and import a small .srt over the API (subtitle import has no UI yet),
then through the browser open the inbox, pick 猫 and make its cards, go to
review, reveal and rate "记得", and assert over the API that exactly the rated
card gained a due date.

The server is the real one, started by e2e/serve.mjs on a throwaway data
directory under test-results/ (never the user's KOTOBA_DATA_DIR) that is deleted
with the run. No dictionary, no AI, no network: the term editor accepts a
hand-written gloss, which keeps the fixture dictionary out of this test.

The e2e job is its own CI job with traces and screenshots kept on failure; it is
deliberately not part of `make check`, which stays fast. Run it locally with
`make e2e`.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* fix(e2e): stop the server with the run so CI teardown cannot hang

The smoke test passed on CI and then the job hung for 19 minutes: the server
wrapper spawned uv detached, so uv and python were in their own process group
and kept the inherited stdout open; Playwright's teardown waited on a pipe that
never closed and the job timed out. Spawning in the same group lets Playwright's
process-group kill take the server down, and the job timeout drops to 10
minutes so a future hang fails fast instead of burning the runner.

entry.title: feat(capture): condensed audio, dialogue only, for the commute (#68) …
entry.content:
feat(capture): condensed audio, dialogue only, for the commute (#68) (#144)

`POST /api/sources/{id}/condensed` joins every timed line of a source into one
track: cues closer than `gap_ms` (default 500ms) merge into a single segment
before cutting, so an episode does not turn into hundreds of fragments with a
click at every seam, and a short silence (default 200ms) is inserted between
segments. The build runs as a background job with the JMdict-style progress
snapshot, writes media/condensed/{source_id}.opus (regenerating replaces the old
file only once the new one is complete), and reports how many lines were used
while skipping the ones without a timeline. ffmpeg is still optional: without
it the request fails readably before a job is started, and the video path goes
through the same video_dirs allowlist as subtitle import.

The merge rule is pinned by its own test — it is the difference between
listening to an episode and listening to confetti.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

entry.title: feat(capture): cut the original voice and a still from the video (#67…
entry.content:
feat(capture): cut the original voice and a still from the video (#67) (#143)

A subtitle import can now take a local video path and, per cue, cut the original
audio (opus, with 250ms/500ms padding on both ends because subtitle times are
navigation hints, not audio boundaries) and a still from the cue's midpoint
(the first frame is often a cut or black). Both land in the media directory and
are written to Line.audio_path / screenshot_path. ffmpeg stays an optional
external dependency: without it the import succeeds with text only and says so
in the response. The path is checked against the user's `video_dirs` setting
before anything is read, so a LAN client cannot turn this into a file reader.
Cue work runs through a pool capped at the CPU count, and one cue's failure is
counted in `media_failed` without taking the episode down.

Tests drive the ffmpeg call through an injectable runner and assert the exact
arguments; no real video is needed.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

entry.title: feat(desktop): add the pywebview shell and tray icon (#60) (#142)
entry.content:
feat(desktop): add the pywebview shell and tray icon (#60) (#142)

* build(backend): add the optional desktop extra

The desktop shell (#60) needs pywebview for the window and pystray for the
tray. Both stay behind the new desktop extra so kotoba serve and CI never
install a GUI toolkit.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* feat(desktop): add the pywebview shell and tray icon (#60)

`kotoba desktop` runs the API in this process, waits for /api/health, then opens
a window and a tray icon. The port is picked fresh when 8720 is taken, closing
the window hides it (capture keeps running) while the tray can show it again,
open the data directory, or quit for real. Quitting stops the in-process server,
so uvicorn's lifespan runs the same cleanup `kotoba serve` gets: watchers, hook
and clipboard stop, the database is disposed, and there is no child process to
orphan. pywebview and pystray are imported lazily and only through the optional
`desktop` extra, so a machine without them can still run `kotoba serve`.

The GUI itself is not driven by tests: the shell takes its desktop through a
`DesktopUI` protocol, the tests drive the startup order and the quit path with
fakes, and `LocalServer` is tested for real against a tiny ASGI app.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* fix(desktop): probe ports the way uvicorn's listener binds (#60)

The port test failed on Linux and macOS: after the health request the port
still had a TIME_WAIT connection, and a plain bind() reports that as taken even
though uvicorn (which sets SO_REUSEADDR) could have used it. The probe now sets
SO_REUSEADDR on POSIX to match the listener; on Windows it stays off, where
SO_REUSEADDR would let the probe bind over a live listener.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

entry.title: feat(review): offline review with a mergeable sync model (#59) (#141)
entry.content:
feat(review): offline review with a mergeable sync model (#59) (#141)

* build(frontend): add ts-fsrs for offline scheduling

The phone needs to schedule reviews locally while offline; ts-fsrs is the
JavaScript sibling of the backend's py-fsrs, so both ends can share weights
and desired retention.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* feat(review): offline review with a mergeable sync model (#59)

Offline reviews now append to ReviewLog with a client-generated id, and a card's
FSRS state becomes a replay of those logs in time order, so two devices that
reviewed the same card converge without comparing stability or difficulty. The
merge is idempotent: re-uploading a batch skips known client ids, and a live
review whose response was lost can be retried with the same id through the sync
endpoint. The phone falls back to the cached queue when the server is
unreachable, schedules locally with ts-fsrs using the backend's weights and
desired retention, and flushes its queue on reconnect. Trade-offs, including
what can still be lost, are written down in docs/adr/0004-offline-sync.md.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

entry.title: feat(reader): 漫画阅读视图与整卷 zip 导入 (#139)
entry.content:
feat(reader): 漫画阅读视图与整卷 zip 导入 (#139)

* feat(text): read mokuro volume zips with their page images

The reader cannot put text boxes over a page it does not have. #52 shipped
the .mokuro file only, so imported manga had no page images and no card
screenshots; this takes the other upload option its issue allowed: the whole
volume folder as a zip, with the .mokuro and the images inside.

Pages are matched to images by natural filename order (2.jpg before 10.jpg),
since the .mokuro format does not record image names. A count mismatch is
rejected rather than silently misaligned, macOS resource-fork entries are
ignored, and images are written under media/manga/<uuid>/0001.jpg by our own
naming, never by the archive member's name.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* feat(reader): expose a work's pages with their text boxes

The reader flips through pages, so it needs lines grouped by page rather than
a flat newest-first list. Each block carries its locator box (percentages are
the client's job), whether it is already carded — the ink distinction in the
view — and the page's image when the import had one.

Grouping is a service because it is query logic: one aggregate for encounter
and card counts keeps a 300-page volume to a single query instead of loading
every relation per line. Lines without a page locator (captures, subtitles)
are not part of the reader and are skipped.

Assisted-by: opencode (deepseek-flash)

* refactor(inbox): share the term-building flow with the reader

Japanese manga turn right to left, so that is the default: left arrow (and a
